newsitem.title: UK: Asda bids in 400 mln stg auction - newspaper.
newsitem.headline: Asda bids in 400 mln stg auction - newspaper.

text.p: British supermarket chain ASDA Plc is bidding for Welcome Break, the motorway service areas being auctioned by Granada Group, the television and leisure company, said the Financial Times newspaper.

Asda is believed to be one of four bidders -- thought also to include the venture capital group CinVen -- invited to submit final offers by today for the 21 motorway service areas, it said. The article added the offers are believed to be at least 400 million pounds ($650 million).

A shortlist of six bidders was reduced to four after the auction entered its final round on Monday and Granada is said to have brought forward its expected date for disposal from the end of March to within two weeks, it said.
Granada acquired Welcome Break through its 3.9 billion pound takeover of Forte last year but must sell it for monopoly reasons since it already owns motorway service areas.
The Department of Trade and Industry set a deadline of April 25 for disposal.

National Express, the coach and bus services group, is believed to have failed to make the final round of bidders while supermarket chain Tesco and property group Heron International are believed to have dropped out, said the newspaper.
